source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.First, make sure you have a NFS share available and that you already know the share's IP address, path, username, and password.
2.Login bmc WebUI
3.mkdir /mnt/nfs_mount
4.mount -t nfs 192.168.0.169:/home/opt /mnt/nfs_mount
NFS — < IP to connect for NFS file system>:/<file path>/<image name>
NOTE:192.168.0.169 is the IP address of your NFS server, /home/opt is the path of the share
5. Use df -h confirm whether the mount is successful
6. Image mount using OpenBMC's Web GUI. From the remote console interface, select Media -> Activate, then select Media -> Mount virtual media.
7. In the "Mount Media File from Network" option, enter your NFS share path, for example: 192.168.0.169:/home/opt/myIMAGE.img
8. From the "Local Media Mounted" section, select your software format (probably CD/DVD), then click "Browse" to find the software file, click "Open", then click "Mount".
9.Once it's done, you can go into the mounted ISO and do things like install an operating system.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: NFS share/URL with a reachable NFS image + BMC web + OS block tools
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Mount image via NFS: mount the install image via NFS from the BMC web -> Media -> Mount Virtual Media (NFS share/URL: ${VM_SHARE:?operator must set the virtual media share or server url}/${VM_PATH:?operator must set the path on the share}/${VM_IMAGE:?operator must set the image file name}), then confirm the image appears as a boot/block device sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsblk 2>&1; dmesg | tail -n 15 2>&1"; state-changing mount.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the OS block-device list + BMC web mount status so the user confirms the NFS image mounted cleanly and is accessible.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: mounting an image shares it to the host and can autostart the OS; use a user-designated image URL and unmount after.

original_test_intent: Validate NFS-backed BMC remote-console virtual media and host CD-ROM exposure; the source also requires an Auto-install program to appear but does not distinguish visibility, boot-to-installer or an actual installation.
original_method: Mount a hard-coded example NFS export on a host, log into BMC WebUI, activate/mount the network image through Remote Console, inspect host visibility and potentially enter an operating-system installer.
manual_activity: Engineering must choose the intended end state. Under a corrected mount-only plan, an operator controls BMC WebUI/Remote Console; boot or installation needs distinct authorization, target-disk ownership and recovery.
required_inputs: engineer-approved mount-only, boot or installation scope
actual NFS server/export/image path and immutable hash
approved NFS version, export permissions, network identity and security model
isolated SUT, boot-order baseline and protected target-disk inventory
BMC virtual-media SOP, expected device identity and console evidence
deactivation, host unmount and recovery plan
safety_requirements: Do not use `192.168.0.169:/home/opt` unless the project explicitly approves that exact export; do not assume username/password semantics for NFS.
Do not boot, auto-install, repartition or write storage until the target disk and destructive scope are explicitly approved.
Baseline devices, mounts and boot order and use read-only export/media semantics where supported.
Reject `sshpass` and disabled SSH host verification; OS evidence must use trusted access.
Deactivate virtual media and unmount the NFS client view after collection; stop on unexpected installer, boot, device or cleanup state without retry.
agent_execution_scope: No execution until the scope, export and safety contract are resolved.
For an approved mount-only flow, validate export/image metadata and collect trusted read-only BMC, console and exact device evidence around the operator action.
Do not operate WebUI, start boot/installation, modify storage or set the final verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve the intended acceptance end state and replace the example export only in a Project Override/recommendation, not Master source.
Approve export security, image identity, target protection, operator sequence, cleanup and recovery.
Execute the attended action and issue the final PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its parameterized path and `lsblk`/short-log check do not define NFS export security, prove Remote Console behavior, distinguish mount from installer coverage or ensure cleanup; the SSH handling is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: None until engineering resolves the end state. For mount-only, use the approved NFS export and vendor WebUI/SOP, record immutable image identity and full before/after device state, then explicitly deactivate and unmount.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The hard-coded NFS example, WebUI sequence, Auto-install wording, incomplete Criteria numbering and 15/5-minute values remain preserved source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Separate NFS reachability/export policy, Remote Console access, BMC virtual-media mount, exact host CD-ROM exposure and cleanup into checkpoints; authorize boot-to-installer or OS installation separately with target-disk protection.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC/WebUI with documented NFS virtual-media support and an approved export security model.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC, WebUI/browser, NFS server/client, image and host OS/tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor virtual-media procedure, NFS export security policy and Project install/recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the fixed example only at project level and separates reversible mount evidence from boot/install actions while preserving Master text.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Mount/visibility does not prove boot or installation; installer appearance alone does not prove a safe or successful install.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Scope decision, export/image contract, disk protection and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: NFS exposure and bootable media can broaden network access or lead to unapproved storage writes.

project_override_considerations: A Project SPEC may approve mount-only coverage and state that boot/install was not verified. It must document the actual export, security mode, image, expected device and cleanup. Any installation requires an explicit disk target, Expected Result and recovery plan.
expected_evidence: approved end state, isolated SUT and protected storage/boot baseline
actual NFS export/security metadata and immutable image hash
BMC WebUI/Remote Console mount transcript and session status
trusted pre/post device and mount inventory identifying the exact virtual CD-ROM
deactivation and NFS unmount, restored host/BMC health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source mixes a local example NFS mount, BMC virtual-media control and possible OS installation. Criteria skip numbered requirements and make an Auto-install program part of acceptance without defining whether it must merely appear, boot or write a target disk.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Reversible media exposure and destructive installation have incompatible core operations and safety contracts. This is not merely a missing export address; engineering must select and authorize the intended end state before execution.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes PARTIAL to BLOCKED because generic device evidence cannot resolve installation intent or NFS/export safety.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and retains its export, image, target-disk and cleanup controls while making Project Override coverage explicit.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Confirms the semantic blocker but corrects next-row provenance and the Round 02 classification from its archived draft.

review_improvement: Separates NFS export validity, BMC mount behavior, host exposure and installation into evidenceable scopes and prevents a hard-coded example from being executed as a target.
independent_technical_reasoning: The exact NFS export is a normal project input, but the source's transition from mounting media to an Auto-install program changes the core safety and acceptance semantics. A read-only `lsblk` result cannot settle that. Until engineering selects mount-only, boot or installation and protects the target, execution would require guessing potentially destructive intent, so the review is BLOCKED rather than PARTIAL.
